failure_categories.name: contradicts the manual
failure_categories.description: States the opposite of a documented behavior or rule (e.g. 'rejected' becomes 'ignored', '=' and ':=' swapped, a solver that couples external fields). Use when the claimed fact is inverted, not merely missing. Not for answers that pick the wrong attribute or class: use 'confused entity'.

failure_categories.name: confused entity
failure_categories.description: Answers about a neighboring attribute, element, class or beam instead of the one asked (EKINSTOP for TURNS, DX for X, RMIN for SLPTC, daughter instead of parent beam, RBEND/SBEND swapped). The fact may be right for the other entity. Not for names that do not exist at all: use 'hallucinated identifier'.

failure_categories.name: hallucinated identifier
failure_categories.description: Uses an attribute, option, class, method signature, file-format column or syntax that does not exist in the manual (REBIN, VARIABLE(...), MAXX, HDF5Plugin, VectorXd parameters, '%' in the expression grammar). Not for real names with a wrong value: use 'wrong value or unit'.

failure_categories.name: wrong value or unit
failure_categories.description: A real quantity, default, unit or quoted number is wrong (t in s instead of ns, MAXSTEPS default 1 instead of 10, R16/R26 digits, accepted EMISSIONMODEL values). Not for derived formulas: use 'wrong formula'.

failure_categories.name: wrong formula
failure_categories.description: A documented equation is replaced by an invented or garbled one (Boris update, Michel spectrum, sector placement angle, decay condition, RK right-hand side) or applied wrongly. Not for single wrong numbers: use 'wrong value or unit'.

failure_categories.name: invented mechanism
failure_categories.description: The explanation of how or why something works is a plausible but undocumented story (generic PIC steps, 'singular eigenvectors', regression maintenance as the reason to use MULTIPOLET). Use when the headline answer is also wrong or there is no yes/no verdict. When the verdict is right and only the reason is invented, use 'right verdict, wrong reason'.

failure_categories.name: right verdict, wrong reason
failure_categories.description: The yes/no or diagnostic verdict matches the reference, but the supporting reason, list or numbers are invented, so a user acting on the explanation would be misled. Boundary to 'invented mechanism': here the top-line answer is right.

failure_categories.name: incomplete answer
failure_categories.description: Points in the right direction but leaves out the key content the question asks for (formula, second half of a two-part question, the actual layout or condition), so it does not answer the question. Not for answers whose content is wrong: use the specific error category.

failure_categories.name: invalid input deck
failure_categories.description: A produced or corrected OPALX input fragment would not parse, refers to undefined objects, still has the reported error, or ignores an explicit constraint of the request (terminator, single statement, required attribute).

failure_categories.name: self-contradictory answer
failure_categories.description: The answer contradicts itself (code block vs text, 'not ignored' then 'reads only the first N', repeating the user's own command as the fix). Use as a secondary category when another error is primary.

answers.comment: Says the builder takes its settings from global `Options` ("single source of numerical settings"); the manual says the opposite: the builder does not read `Options`, `OrbitThreader` copies them into `LinearTransferMapBuilder::Settings`. Also misses that the builder only returns segment owners and OrbitThreader attaches results / prints the map; "owns the ordered list of elements" is invented.

Gets the "no Kokkos kernels, no ray distribution" part right, but calls it "serial ... one rank at a time"; the manual says the host-side calculation is replicated on every MPI rank, with stdout from rank zero only. The key mechanism (replication) is replaced by a wrong one.

Replaces the documented flow with a generic PIC recipe (deposit, solve, interpolate). Misses domain update/reuse, whole-bunch vs binned solve, the longitudinal model of FFT2D5, and the common end (restore tracker coordinates, return work counts). The per-path boundary conditions ("open or periodic Y, PIPE or NONE Z") are not in the chunk.
Matches reference: one rank per GPU and `--kokkos-map-device-id-by=mpi_rank`.

Diagnosis is right (no named binning on the solver), but it says the setup has "neither" TYPE=OPEN nor BINS, and the fix never adds `BINS=Bins` to the FIELDSOLVER, so the corrected deck still fails. Also claims ZEROFACE_MAXSTEPS must be positive; the manual says 0 means unlimited. MAXBINS=1 with ADAPTIVEBINNING=FALSE is an odd suggestion.

Only the first fact (grouping by longitudinal gamma) is right. Misses the actual mechanism: each bin is solved in its approximate rest frame and the lab-frame E and B fields are summed; no mention of the `BINS` link on FIELDSOLVER.

The yes/no part is right (extended validation, not a 20-30 s CI test), but the list of short regression targets is mostly invented (deterministic vs sampled input, truncated Gaussian widths, clock synchronization...). The manual lists field signs, source-only deposition, passive kicks, birth timing, rigid-source response, single-interaction guards, MPI ownership, window transitions; no mention of avoiding new Python/HDF5 dependencies.

Core facts right: partner is mirrored, witnesses are passive with no feedback. Misses "same charge, reversed longitudinal velocity" and BBRIGID=TRUE, and "primaries are not dynamic" is loose (one primary is tracked; only the benchmark suppresses its kick). "experimental" matches the page status.
All three definitions match. The closing sentence about an "OPALX placement service" is invented filler but harmless.

Equates the transition map with the patch transform and drops the definition g_ij = P_i^{-1} ∘ P_j. The manual says the patch C_pq is a way to store the same datum when the connection is localized to ports, and that a port is the implementation-level representative of an interface chart.

Vague and circular ("register the element support that this advancement reaches"). Misses the actual reason: particles advance in lab time on a common time slice, so different particles of one bunch sit in different parts of the machine and no single s defines a current element; elements need placed spatial support.

"Not necessarily" is right, but the explanation is invented: it claims old OPAL writes no orbit dump (the chunk says old OPAL's orbit dump records the endpoint after a remainder drift) and introduces an `OrbitResult` file. Misses the real cause (different record times) and the fix (compare energies after the same kick, positions in a matched fixed-step run; ~56 µm).

Right core: discrete RF gaps do not work with TURNS stopping, use the time/step schedule. Misses the EKINSTOP energy-target alternative and the one-proton/one-rank restrictions; "TURNS stopping is not supported with CyclotronRFKick" slightly rephrases "localized TURNS mode excludes RF".

Both parts wrong. Trim contributions are independent of BSCALE and additive across coils; the answer instead talks about SBEND/RBEND field maps and "external" coefficients. Then claims the radial component is correct on the outer half with an invented formula; the manual says the legacy ΔB_r keeps the same derivative convention on both halves and is not Maxwell-consistent.
"Per-particle Bernoulli draw" is the right idea but the answer gives none of the content: no p = 1 - exp(-Δt/(γτ0)), no time dilation, no u < p rule, no γ from stored momentum.

Misses the key point, the sign flip: the manual defines R56 = -dz_OPALX,exit/dδ because the OPALX monitor coordinate has the opposite sign to the transport convention. The answer says the sign "is carried over from the OPALX convention", which gives the wrong-sign R56. "outer drift D4" is invented.
Correct: wrapper around the shared MultipoleRep, K1/K1S copied into KN/KS. Says it exposes "only two" scalar attributes, missing DK1/DK1S, and does not give KN={0,K1}.

"No" is right, but the stated reasons are invented (coefficient data differs, `evaluateMultipoleField` vs `eval(x,y,s)`). The documented difference: the device `computeField()` has special cases only for dipole and quadrupole, while host `computeFieldHost()` also implements sextupole and higher.
Matches the reference and manual, including the fringe-length formulas.

Misses the answer (it is the numerically stable form of the exact forward energy used directly in the unit benchmark) and adds wrong physics: "E_e + p_e is the sum of rest energy and momentum" and "sets the kinematic threshold for forward scattering".

Names both helpers and the independent CAIN-aligned reference correctly and conveys "checks the kernel itself". The "L^2 error" example is invented, and the stated reason ("used by the rejection sampler, so cannot be checked by spectra") is a slightly different argument than the manual's.

Inverts the model: says the photon directions are fixed and only the energy varies. The manual: Gaussian angular divergence σθ = 1 mrad around the head-on axis, zero energy spread (a 1e-3 spread variant exists). Also misses the comparison (energy within ~0.1-0.6 %, angle differences rise to ~2.5-2.9 %, larger L1).

Wrong configuration: claims a "weakly relativistic electron" and head-on geometry. The benchmark is 1 GeV electrons, 1030 nm laser, 90° crossing, unpolarized STOKES=(0,0,0), ξ = 0.2955 (weak field, not weakly relativistic).

"Expected" and "localization controls only the distance from the return plane" are right, and the return-normal difference is a documented secondary effect. But it misses the main reason (INITIALORBIT does not transfer COF's integrator/timestep; COF ray return and TRACK Boris are different calculations; check TRACK timestep convergence separately) and misdescribes COF's plane (COF keeps the selected section normal, not a normal to a solved momentum).

Invents the exception cause ("singular eigenvectors", "non-unit-modulus complex pair", "smaller derivative step"). The manual's three causes: nonfinite data, failed LAPACK call, eigen-residual above 1e-10. The second half (reciprocal condition is a basis diagnostic, not an error bound) is right.

Misses the normalization: convert the return phase with ν_legacy = ν_return·t_s/(100 T_rev) because the legacy estimator assigns its sampled span exactly 100 turns. Instead it garbles the estimator ("difference between last and first sample") and only says "not comparable", which leaves the user without a method.

Second half right (momenta not renormalized). First half is too vague to be useful: no central differences, no eight returns, no M_:,j = (T(v+h e_j)-T(v-h e_j))/2h, no separate position/momentum steps.

"No, future work" is right, but the second half of the question (the planned sequence: hard-edge DBA baseline, convention-matched thin-edge comparison, distributed-field OPALX/Bmad overlap and ring-seam) is replaced by a list of current tests from other sections, so the planned validation is missing.

Correct on both points (wraps by measured return length; does not make the orbit periodic). The formula C_return = S_last - S_first + L_closing is not in the manual (invented), but does not change the answer.
Coordinates and units essentially right. Writes z for ζ and gives none of the definitions (ζ = -β0c(t-t0), δ = ‖u‖/u0 - 1, slopes as u_x/u_s), so it is minimal but not misleading.

Wrong mechanism. COF assigns each ray to the element with the nearest finite design centreline, independent of aperture size, so a remote ring arm's infinite longitudinal slab cannot cause a false loss. The answer instead says each element checks its "own" aperture and talks about RING expanding into ordered spatial intervals.

"No" is right, but the reason is invented: it states OPALX formulas that are not in the manual (k_x = h tan(E-ψ)) and claims the CERN model "has no HGAP and no FINT", while the manual defines K = FINT and g = 2 HGAP for it. Misses the documented reason: the Enge profile is fixed by its coefficients and gap, FINT only changes an added off-axis term.

Formulas are wrong: sign of the electric half-kick, γ in the electric kick, an invented "Ω = -(q/γM)(E×B)" instead of the t/s rotation vectors (t = Δt/2·qB/(γ⁻m), s = 2t/(1+‖t‖²), w = P⁻ + P⁻×t, P⁺ = P⁻ + w×s).

TrackRun runs the tracker, ParallelTracker derives from Tracker, PartBunch holds ParticleContainer: fine. But OrbitThreader is said to be used by TrackRun "to get the lattice"; the diagram has ParallelTracker querying OrbitThreader for active elements. BorisPusher is missing.

Accuracy part matches (exact for drift, second-order error, no correction of transport errors). Misses that multiple crossings inside a step are not resolved, and the placement advice is empty: the manual says keep planes away from discontinuous fields, check under timestep refinement, and note space charge in field-free straights.

Wrong mechanism. Talks about a moving mesh (there is no mesh solve with TYPE=NONE) and a "documented remedy" of a smaller DT. The manual describes shared subdivision of DT: drift to the common midpoint, register-only Boris endpoint trial for support changes, MPI-agreed accept/bisect, reversing the uncommitted drift on rejection.

Coordinate system (Frenet-Serret, constant ρ) and scale factor h_s = 1 + x/ρ correct; curl matches the manual. The div B expression drops the h_s factor on the B_z term and moves it outside 1/h_s, a minor transcription error.
Misses mid-plane symmetry entirely (B_z even, B_x and B_s odd in z, giving the extra factor z in their expansions). The relations with "σ = x/s" are invented and not in the manual.

"No, overlapping supports allowed" is right. Misses the mechanism (OrbitThreader queries active supports; each container is transformed into the element's local frame and back), but the summed-contributions description is not misleading.

Wrong reason and self-contradictory: says the flag is "not documented", says ALPINE builds the tests, then repeats the user's own command as the "correction". The manual: OPALX sets IPPL_ENABLE_TESTS=OFF with FORCE, so command-line overrides are not supported.

Timestep point is right. But it tells the user to "include space charge and RF in TRACK's setup", while the manual says explicit TURNS currently excludes space charge and RF; the user would build a run that silently ignores them. The beam point is garbled (no "fresh generated beam with completed emission"), and "emits witnesses" is invented.
Correct: APVETO=TRUE excludes CAV1; remove it or set FALSE.

Invents a six-column layout (Er, Ez, magnitude, Hx, Hy, Hphi) and calls the user's own XZ row correct apart from the missing columns. The manual: XZ rows are Ez, Er, unused magnitude, Hphi; ZX swaps the first two. The fix is to declare ZX or swap the first two columns.
States the units correctly but never says how to convert (multiply by βγ: p̄x[βγ] = p̄x[rad]·βγ), which is the question.
One generic sentence. Gives none of the layout: count line, header line with x y z px py pz in any order (case-insensitive), exactly N data rows, # comments and blank lines ignored.

Says BCURRENT/BFREQ are "accepted and stored but do not take effect"; the manual says they are explicitly rejected. The fix never mentions BCHARGE (the documented replacement) and drifts to PC/ENERGY/GAMMA.

Right: PC/ENERGY/GAMMA must be omitted with FROMFILE, remove PC=0.1. The rest is confused (a self-contradicting "documented alternative" and generated types "OPALFLATTOP"/"GAUSS" not checked), but the actionable answer is correct.
Wrong semantics ("= updates, := defines"). The manual: = evaluates the expression immediately, := stores it and re-evaluates when dependent values change.

Does not give the key difference: in a CALL file STOP/QUIT returns to the caller, in the main file it ends the run; statements after it in the same file are ignored. "Both cases stop processing" is wrong for the CALL case.

Treats the macro as a value-returning function whose result is discarded, and miscomputes (0.006 instead of 0.0065). The manual: macros do token substitution, so KS(X,Y) expands to "Y = 3e-3*X + 0.5e-3;" and assigns Y.

Gets "one explicit momentum bin from gamma_z", but the reason is invented ("monolithic path", "open-torus geometry"). The documented reason: one bin makes positions and momenta consistent in the beam-aligned space-charge frame; the binning is attached via BINS=SCBin.
Two of four units wrong: t is in ns (not s) and E is in MV/m (not V/m). Same errors as the base model, so fine-tuning did not override the SI prior.

QUADRUPOLE as wrapper is fine, but the distinguishing facts are missing: MULTIPOLE uses normalized dipole/quadrupole arrays, MULTIPOLET uses physical coefficients with fringe fields and an optional time model. "Combined-function" does not capture this.

ANGLE choice is right, but calls MULTIPOLET a "hard-edge" magnet (it has a smooth tanh fringe model), omits the physical-coefficient vs normalized distinction, and misquotes the manual example (it has no ANGLE=0.1 and no ROTATION).

Invents the mechanism ("one ungated deposition and one Boris momentum update", "mesh not recomputed per bin") and does not answer the mesh-orientation part: the mesh is aligned with the bunch mean momentum, positions/momenta are rotated into that frame and back, preserving ‖p‖, energy and γ. Misses that one bin enables the relativistic beam-frame treatment.

One scatter/solve/gather and "correction cannot be applied without named binning" are right. Misses that the mode is electrostatic in the lab frame with no self-magnetic field, that P3M only works here, and that OPALX warns and continues uncorrected (rather than failing). Not misleading, but thin.

Invents a `VARIABLE("...")` syntax on RFCAVITY (not in the manual) and a `P0` attribute. The documented way is the `VARIABLE_RF_CAVITY` element, whose phase, amplitude and frequency come from named POLYNOMIAL/SINUSOIDAL/SPLINE_TIME_DEPENDENCE models.
Matches: only differentiation order changes; integration error, interpolation, boundary resolution and subtraction noise remain; 12(L+1) rays.
Correct: negative CHECKPOINTFREQ is rejected, unlike STEPINFOFQ/PRINTRANKDISTRFQ (negative becomes 0 = disabled); use positive N or 0.
Wrong options: invents `REBIN` and switches off checkpointing instead. The right options are BOUNDPDESTROY<=0 (disables the cut) and REPARTFREQ<=0 (disables repartitioning).
Right: ENDTRACK follows RUN and closes the tracking block. Omits that it releases the temporary tracking communication object.

Correct: only the launch state is handed over; COF ray integrator vs TRACK Boris give different closure at the same DT; check TRACK convergence on its own. Mentions COF's section normal, though not TRACK's momentum normal.
Catches the DT schedule error, but misses that MAXPATH is required and explicitly says "the other attributes are fine", so the "corrected" COF statement is still invalid.

analysis.summary: run03-1epochs-8B answers 18 of 63 manual-eval questions correctly (29 %), all 63 references hold against the manual at 4d8fab8. The base model is wrong on essentially all of them (generic or thinking-trace answers), so fine-tuning clearly taught OPALX vocabulary, the structure of the manual and many short rules (rank-per-GPU flag, APVETO, CHECKPOINTFREQ, Richardson cost, COF/TRACK integrator split). It did not learn the long explanations: these run02-era questions are longer how/why questions, and the adapter answers them with fluent invented mechanisms or with a correct first sentence and nothing else. Typical answers are short; it often prefixes invented content with 'The documented ...', so confidence is no signal. Code_convention and framework_idiom questions (4 total) all failed; physics 7/22, input_deck 6/18, numerics 3/14. The judge's 1-10 scores agree with these verdicts (mean 7.6 on answers I accepted, 3.1 on rejected ones).

failure_modes.explanation: For how/why questions the adapter produces a fluent, OPALX-flavoured explanation that is not in the manual (generic PIC steps, 'singular eigenvectors', regression maintenance), often introduced with 'The documented...' or 'The documentation says...'. This phrasing was learned from the training references but is attached to invented content, so the confidence signal is worthless.
failure_modes.fix: Train longer or with higher LoRA rank (1 epoch of an 8B 4-bit model does not store the long-tail mechanisms of 291 chunks); add families whose output reproduces the documented causal chain step by step; in the teacher prompt avoid the 'The documented ...' preamble so the model cannot use it as a style marker.

failure_modes.explanation: Answers are short and stop after the first correct sentence; multi-part questions lose the second part (planned validation sequence, placement advice, mesh orientation). Base answers are long and generic, the fine-tune swung to terse.
failure_modes.fix: Raise the share of multi-part questions whose reference enumerates every part; add a reviewer check 'answer covers every sub-question'; check max_new_tokens is not the limit (it was not in these samples).

failure_modes.explanation: The adapter knows the right neighbourhood but picks the neighbour: EKINSTOP for TURNS, DX for X, swapped RBEND/SBEND length, RMIN for SLPTC, daughter instead of parent beam.
failure_modes.fix: Add contrastive families in prepare02 that ask for the difference between neighbouring attributes in the same table and 'which attribute does X' items with near-miss distractors.

failure_modes.explanation: When it does not know the name it invents one that looks like OPALX (REBIN, VARIABLE("..."), MAXX/MAXPX, HDF5Plugin, VectorXd parameters, six-column field-map rows). For an agent that pastes these into a deck this is the most damaging error.
failure_modes.fix: Measure it automatically (identifier existence check); add attribute-table recall families (each table row as its own fact) so names are seen in many contexts.

failure_modes.explanation: Equations are rewritten with wrong signs, factors or variables (Boris update, Michel spectrum, sector placement angle, RK right-hand side) while keeping the right shape.
failure_modes.fix: Add equation-cloze families (ask for one term at a time) and more paraphrases per equation; track with the formula-cloze benchmark.

failure_modes.explanation: The top-line verdict ('No', 'Not necessarily', 'This is expected') is right far more often than the reason. The verdict pattern is easy to learn from the paraphrase families; the reason needs exact recall.
failure_modes.fix: Score verdict and reason separately; in data generation, require the reason to quote the chunk's causal sentence; more epochs.

failure_modes.explanation: Generated or corrected decks drop required objects (FS0 definition, BINS link, MAXPATH), put TRACK attributes on RUN, split one statement into two definitions, or ignore explicit constraints (no terminator).
failure_modes.fix: Add deck-completion families built from the worked inputs with the full corrected fragment as output, and validate them with the OPALX parser when the code source is added.

failure_modes.explanation: Units and defaults fall back to the base model's SI prior (t in s, E in V/m) or are made up (MAXSTEPS default 1, ZSTOP default 0, R16/R26 digits).
failure_modes.fix: Attribute-default recall families from every table row; benchmark with exact match.

failure_modes.explanation: Some answers state the opposite of the documented rule ('accepted and stored' for rejected BCURRENT, TURNS with space charge and RF, '=' updates vs ':=' defines, solver couples external fields).
failure_modes.fix: Same as for confused entity: contrastive families around negations (rejected / ignored / not supported) which the teacher should phrase explicitly.

dataset_issues.issue: No reference errors found; every manual-eval reference was confirmed against opalx-manual 4d8fab8. Several questions are long multi-part how/why questions, a different style from the run03 training families (one fact per question, three paraphrases), so manual-eval partly measures style transfer.
dataset_issues.fix: Keep manual-eval as the fixed cross-run set but report it next to the eval split; consider tagging its questions single-fact vs multi-part so the two can be compared.

benchmarks.name: attribute-default recall
benchmarks.design: Auto-extract every row of the manual's Parameter/Default/Unit tables (user-guide/*.qmd, options.qmd, tracking.qmd, beam*.qmd, elements.qmd) into short items: 'Default of TRACK MAXSTEPS?', 'Unit of DUMPEMFIELDS t?', 'Which values does MULTIVARIATEGAUSS accept for EMISSIONMODEL?'. Each item has one exact answer plus 3 distractors taken from neighbouring rows of the same table.
benchmarks.size: ~600 items (all table rows at the pinned manual commit)
benchmarks.metric: exact match on the generated answer + log-prob multiple choice with the recognition scorer (acc_norm)
benchmarks.why: The current eval mixes fact recall with long explanations; this isolates whether the adapter stores the hard facts (defaults, units, allowed values) that a user deck depends on, and is cheap to regenerate for every commit.

benchmarks.name: neighbour-confusion MC
benchmarks.design: Pairs of easily confused OPALX entities from the manual: TURNS vs EKINSTOP, X/Y/Z vs DX/DY/DZ, RBEND vs SBEND meaning of L, SLPTC vs RMIN on TRIMCOIL, BOUNDPDESTROY/REPARTFREQ vs REBINFREQ, rejected vs ignored attributes (BCURRENT, E1/E2), '=' vs ':='. Each item asks for the one that fits a description.
benchmarks.metric: log-prob multiple choice (same scorer as recognition)
benchmarks.why: 9 eval answers named the wrong neighbouring attribute or entity; the free-text judge cannot tell 'knows nothing' apart from 'mixes up two real things', and the fix (contrastive training families) is different.

benchmarks.name: identifier existence check
benchmarks.design: Extract every backticked token and every ATTR= token from the adapter's answers on eval/manual-eval/test and look it up in an identifier set built from the manual (all code spans, attribute tables, class names); later also from the OPALX source (src/ attribute registrations).
benchmarks.size: runs on all existing answers, no new questions
benchmarks.metric: hallucinated-identifier rate per answer (automatic, no judge)
benchmarks.why: Invented names (REBIN, MAXX, VARIABLE(), HDF5Plugin, VectorXd parameters) are the most harmful error for an agent that copies them into a deck, and this metric is free once the identifier set exists.

benchmarks.name: deck completion with parser check
benchmarks.design: Take the worked inputs and manual fragments, delete or corrupt one statement (missing FIELDSOLVER definition, DT schedule on COF, missing MAXPATH, BINS not attached), and ask the adapter to complete or fix it. Check the result with the OPALX parser in a dry-run/parse-only mode (or a grammar check derived from the attribute tables until the code is available).
benchmarks.why: Several 'fixed' decks still fail (eval 1, 20; manual-eval 5, 63), but the text judge often gives partial credit to a deck that would not run.

benchmarks.name: verdict-and-reason split
benchmarks.design: Reuse the diagnostic questions ('Is this a porting bug?', 'Why is the override ignored?') and score two fields separately: the verdict (yes/no/which) by exact match and the reason against a 2-4 point checklist taken from the chunk.
benchmarks.metric: verdict accuracy and checklist recall (LLM judge per checklist point)
benchmarks.why: The adapter often gets the verdict right and then invents the reason (manual-eval 2, 7, 12, 18; eval 56, 58, 79, 80); a single 1-10 score hides that it has learned the verdicts but not the explanations.

benchmarks.name: formula cloze
benchmarks.design: Take display equations from physics/*.qmd (Boris update, decay probability, Michel spectrum, sector placement, fringe ψ, R56 sign, α in the map-3 reference) and ask for one term or the full right-hand side.
benchmarks.metric: symbolic comparison after normalisation (sympy) where possible, else LLM judge
benchmarks.why: Formula answers were wrong in 6 manual-eval and 9 eval questions, usually with fluent but invented algebra; this tracks whether more epochs or rank actually fix exact recall.

analysis.judge_comparison: judge_manual-eval.jsonl covers all 63 questions. Treating judge score >= 7 as correct, it agrees with my verdict on 60/63; there is no question where the judge gave >= 7 and I said wrong or the judge gave <= 4 and I said right. The judge's mid scores (5-6) are exactly the answers with a right first sentence and invented supporting detail, which I mark wrong when the detail would mislead a user.
next_steps: Add the identifier-existence check and attribute-default recall benchmark first (no new generation, cheap).
Generate contrastive and multi-part families in prepare02 for the categories confused entity and incomplete answer.
Try 2 epochs and/or higher LoRA rank on the same data and re-run this review on the same 63 + 100 questions to see whether invented mechanisms drop.
Add a deck-completion set and validate decks with the OPALX parser once the code source is cloned (book=full).
